source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Sion tops the poll: rural elections with 96 pc"); Irish News, 2 June 1967, p. 1 ("96 per cent turned out at Strabane"); Irish News, 17 May 1967, p. 8 (nominations: "Coleraine")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page images (council-audit, Nov 2026): Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 'Slaught—C. R. Lee 207; W. W. Houston 173'; Irish News, 17 May 1967, p. 8 nominations 'Slaght—W. W. Huston, and C. R. Lee'.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1967. Two of the 21 seats were contested; the other divisions were filled unopposed and their names were not printed in the reports used here. This is the Slaght division (Irish News nominations; the Belfast Telegraph prints 'Slaught'); the file's name 'Slaughtneil' is a mistake. Lee elected; Houston was the retiring member; 84 pc poll.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of the Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 and the Irish News, 17 May 1967, p. 8 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the division is Slaght (printed 'Slaught' in the Telegraph), not Slaughtneil; the nomination notice added to the citation. The file and index name are left for the lander to rename.
